chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Muʿādhī, from Muḥammad ibn Bakr, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: Indeed, our companions do something: when they attend the funeral and the burial of the deceased, they do not return until they wipe their hands over the grave. Is that a sunnah (prophetic tradition) or a bidʿah? He said: That is obligatory upon one who did not attend the salat (prayer) over him.

key_terms.الْجِنَازَةَ: the funeral procession or bier of the deceased
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: an established prophetic or religious practice
key_terms.يَمْسَحُوا: they wipe or pass the hands over

ai.seo_question: Is wiping the hands over the grave after burial a sunnah (prophetic tradition) or a bidʿah according to Imam al-Kāẓim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith asks Imam Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about the practice of wiping one’s hands over the grave after attending a burial. The Imam عليه السلام states that this act is obligatory for one who did not attend the funeral salat (prayer) over the deceased, indicating a specific legal ruling connected to burial rites.
